text:
morgan: Heads up — seeing multiple reports of 'egress silence' from gpu-nodepool-usw2 over the past hour. Pods can send requests to shard services but some TCP streams drop after ~1-3k bytes, looks like partial transfers. only affects pods on rack-r12/r13.

sanjay: Any pattern on MTU, overlay or physical links? RDMA nodes?

morgan: Mostly Geneve overlay. Underlay is mlx5 / 100Gb, jumbo MTU 9000. Affected nodes are on the RDMA-enabled subnet.

elaine: Can you paste a tcpdump or ss? quick checks: ip link, ethtool -k, dmesg for offload/kernel drops.

morgan: grabbing dumps now. short tcpdump from pod host -> shard (TCP reset followed by nothing):
```
12:34:21.123456 IP 10.42.3.12.49152 > 10.50.10.4.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:14321, ack 6789, win 32768, length 1976
12:34:21.123789 IP 10.42.3.12.49152 > 10.50.10.4.443: Flags [P.], seq 14321:16330, ack 6789, win 32768, length 2009
12:34:21.124001 IP 10.50.10.4.443 > 10.42.3.12.49152: Flags [.], ack 16330, win 65535, length 0
```
Second packet never hits remote (packet length ~2009).

morgan: ip link show dev geneve0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
ethtool -k eth0 on host: tx-checksumming: on offload: tx-checksumming: on

netbot: [alert] multiple encap checksum errors seen on rack-r13 between 12:20-12:40 UTC (summary: 18 drops)

elaine: That looks like PMTU/fragmentation issue — geneve header + UDP + inner packet pushes outer > underlay MTU but offload hides fragments. Kernel might be dropping oversized encapped frames instead of generating ICMP "Fragmentation needed" because of offload/accelerator.

sanjay: Could also be mlx5 offload + RDMA path switching causing offload miscalc. Can you run `dmesg | grep -i geneve` and `ip -s link show dev eth0`?

morgan: dmesg: "geneve: tx: packet too big (len 9216) — dropping" few repeats.

morgan: ip -s link eth0 shows TX bytes with some errors (GSO fragmented), counters bump when issue occurs.

elaine: Quick mitigation: disable GSO/TSO on the host NIC or lower host MTU so encap fits. Also try disabling tx-checksum offload on geneve device.

devops-oncall: I'm going to apply a non-invasive test on two impacted nodes (rack-r12/r13): set geneve mtu -> 1400 and `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` then monitor for 15m. Will patch 2 nodes at a time. @sanjay FYI.

morgan: repro command I used from pod: `curl -v --max-time 5 https://10.50.10.4:443/healthz` — hanging after sending a chunk.

devops-oncall: applied to rack-r12-03 and rack-r13-07, rolling now. so far 12 requests that previously stalled now complete within 20ms.

elaine: Good sign. We should schedule infra work: either set host MTU to 8980 to accommodate geneve+headers on RDMA paths or add sysctl to force PMTU discovery aggression. Also file vendor ticket for mlx5 firmware/driver interaction with GSO on encap.

morgan: captured kernel log after mitigation: geneve tx errors dropped to 0, and tcpdump shows fragments being handled.

sanjay: Long-term: automate detection for encap oversize errors (dmesg greps) and route vulnerable racks to fallback path (no RDMA offload) until driver fix. Also consider cluster-wide geneve mtu config via CNI.

devops-oncall: I'll open a runbook step and schedule a firmware validation window next week. For now marking as mitigated. :white_check_mark:

morgan: Thanks — leaving this thread for follow-ups. saved tcpdumps to s3://redwood-debug/vxlan-egress-silence/2177654321/

netbot: [monitor] no new encap drops reported in last 30m on racks r12-r13

elaine: follow-ups: (1) vendor ticket #RDMA-2841 (driver+offload), (2) CNI PR to set geneve mtu default 1400, (3) alert rule for 'geneve: tx: packet too big' in kernel logs.

morgan: noted. I'll add the PR and attach dumps to the ticket.

sanjay: nice triage team. if it resurfaces, prioritize a kernel/driver test matrix on a staging rack with rdma on/off.
